brief.label: Briefed
brief.demo: Both pilots state the agreement back in their own words — who does what, and when.
brief.gate: Advance when it is said out loud by both of you. An assumed agreement is not one; the point of the brief is to find the places where you each assumed something different.

locate.label: Located — no hunting
locate.demo: Partner names the control; you put a finger on it and say its name back. No narrating the search, no sweeping the panel.
locate.gate: First touch correct, inside about two seconds, three times running from different starting hand positions. A correct find after a visible search is a miss — note it and come back to it before the block ends.

recall.label: Recalled — exact
recall.demo: You state the value and its unit from memory, out loud, before looking at any gauge, page or card.
recall.gate: Exact number and exact unit on the first attempt. "About 290" is a bust, and so is a self-corrected guess. Miss it and the card goes on tonight's re-drill list; do not keep grinding it in the seat.

verbatim.label: Verbatim — 100%
verbatim.demo: Challenge and response, word for word, in the published order, out loud — with your hands reaching the actual switch as the words come out.
verbatim.gate: No prompting, no reordering, no paraphrase, and the hands must not lag the words. Anything less and you run the whole drill again from the top — not from the step you missed. Partner logs it and says nothing until the flow finishes.

flow.label: Flow — unprompted
flow.demo: The complete sequence, in order, with every confirmation actually read off the display page it lives on — not assumed.
flow.gate: No checklist prompting on the flow itself, and no skipped confirmation. Wording may flex; sequence and the confirmations may not. Two clean runs before you call it done.

operate.label: Operated — and read back
operate.demo: You make the selection in the device, then read the resulting indication aloud — synoptic page, CAS, annunciator, whichever the system answers on.
operate.gate: Correct selection first time, and the resulting indication named correctly without help. Getting the switch right but not knowing what the screen now says is a miss — that is the half that matters under load.

identify.label: Identified — unaided
identify.demo: Partner triggers or sets the condition without telling you what it is. You name it — by aural, colour, annunciation or synoptic state — before reading its label.
identify.gate: Correct name before the label is read, with no hints. If you needed the label, that one goes on the re-drill list.

explain.label: Explained — no notes
explain.demo: You explain the logic to your partner in your own words, with nothing in front of you: what the system does, when, and what it does not do.
explain.gate: Partner has the card or the manual open and cannot find a gap or a wrong condition. If they have to fill in a step for you, it is not yet known.

repeat.label: Repeated to fluency
repeat.demo: The repetitions actually happen, back to back, in the seat.
repeat.gate: The last repetition is at least as clean and at least as fast as the first. If it is getting worse you are tired — stop the block and note it, because grinding a degrading drill trains the error.

trap.label: Trap caught
trap.demo: Partner deliberately sets or walks you into the error without warning. You catch it, stop, and say what the trap was.
trap.gate: Caught before the consequence, and named out loud. Catching it silently is half credit — naming it is what makes it stick. Missed it? Reset and let them spring it again later in the session, not immediately.

swap.label: Repeated from the other seat
swap.demo: The other pilot now flies it, to the same standard the block already set. You take the monitoring and checklist role.
swap.gate: Advance when the second pilot meets the standard unaided — not when they have watched you do it. Both of you need this from both seats; the start flow in particular is asymmetric.

note.label: Nothing to demonstrate
note.demo: Nothing to perform — this line sets how the block is run, or tells you where its limit is.
note.gate: Read it, agree it, tick it. It is on the list so the standard is explicit rather than assumed.

log.label: Written down
log.demo: The list physically exists — paper, notes app, anything you will still have tonight.
log.gate: Written, not remembered. This is the block that feeds tomorrow's drilling, so "I'll recall it later" fails the standard.
